- When sentiment is consistently negative or neutral over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns negative after a rally, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 3–5 days post-sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is weak or mixed, especially if recent history shows mean reversion; add 1–3% to forecast to account for reversion bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits short-term momentum; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast tail (last 3–5 days).
- If sentiment is positive but price history shows no recent uptrend, model may overreact; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid false momentum bias.
